rows.acip: TSE BLOS GTONG ZHES PA'I BLOS GTONG RGYU'I GTZO BO 'DI SNANG CHOS BRGYAD KYI ZHEN PA DE BLOS THONG BA DGOS, DE THONGS NA YO BYAD THAMS CAD GTOR NAS SPRANG PO BYED PA ZHIG NGES PAR MI DGOS TE, DAM PA TSOS TSE BLOS THONGS PA'I TSAD LA RGYAL MCHOG BSKAL BZANG RGYA MTSO DANG , PAn CHEN BLO BZANG YE SHES SOGS 'JOG PAR MDZAD PA YIN,
rows.wylie: tshe blos gtong zhes pa'i blos gtong rgyu'i gtso bo 'di snang chos brgyad kyi zhen pa de blos thong ba dgos, de thongs na yo byad thams cad gtor nas sprang po byed pa zhig nges par mi dgos te, dam pa tshos tshe blos thongs pa'i tshad la rgyal mchog bskal bzang rgya mtsho dang , paN chen blo bzang ye shes sogs 'jog par mdzad pa yin
rows.english: Now when we say to "give up on this life," the main thing that you have to give up is those eight worldly thoughts or attachments, towards the pleasures of this life. Giving up these thoughts doesn't necessarily mean that you have to throw away all your material possessions and become a beggar. Holy teachers of the past have pointed out for us examples of people who succeeded in giving up on life, and these have included personages of fantastic material wealth such as Gyalchok Kelsang Gyatso and the Panchen Lobsang Yeshe.32 21 Lord Maitreya about Giving up on Life

rows.english: The great master of all master meditators, Milarepa, has said as well: If in your heart you wish to keep the holy practice, son, Within the very depths of it then find this thing first--faith, Never turn and look back once again upon--this life. If in truth you'll follow after me, Your loved ones turn to demons, hold you back; Do not think them true--cut all the ties. Food and money are the demons' advance guard; The closer the worse, give up all want for them. The objects of the senses are the demons' snare; "They will entrap me!" stop your craving them. Your young love is the daughter of the demons; "She will mislead me!" so be on your guard. The place you grew up is the demons' prison; Hard to free yourself from, flee it quick. You will have to leave it all behind and go on--later, Why not make it meaningful and leave it all--right now? It will fall down one day anyway, this mannequin apparition; Better to use this body now, get off to a good quick start. This skittish bird of mind will anyway fly from the corpse one day; Better now to soar across some wide expanse of sky. If you listen and act upon this one man's words--of mine, Then the grace to keep the holy practice, my boy--is yours.33 22 Death in the Wild of a Mountain Cave

rows.english: The point here is that, to rid yourself of the eight worldly thoughts and undertake a spiritual practice which is truly pure, you must gain two different realizations: first, of how valuable and hard to find one's life of leisure and fortune is; secondly, of one's own impermanence and the fact that he must die. Once you gain these realizations, it doesn't matter--the hills can turn to gold, the rivers into milk, and every man your slave--but to you it's all repulsive, useless, like a feast set before a sick man vomiting. And it's not enough for these realizations to come to you just from the outside--from sitting and listening to someone describe them. They must come from the inside, from thinking about them yourself. Then they will be firm in your mind, and never change again. 25 How Rare a Life Like This Is

rows.acip: SGYU MA MKHAN GYIS RDE SHING RTA GLANG DU SPRUL BA'I TSE, SNGAGS RDZAS KYIS MIG BSLAD PA'I LTAD MO BA RNAMS LA RDE SHING RTA GLANG DU SNANG BA DANG ZHEN PA GNYIS YOD, SGYU MA MKHAN RANG NYID LA RTA GLANG DU SNANG BA TZAM YOD KYANG , ZHEN PA MED SNGAGS RDZAS KYIS MIG MA BSLAD PA'I PHYIS KYI LTAD MO BA LA RDE SHING RTA GLANG DU SNANG ZHEN GNYIS KA MED PA DE BZHIN DU GZUGS SOGS KYI CHOS RNAMS KYI STENG DU SNANG ZHEN MI 'DRA BA GSUM 'BYUNG STE, STONG NYID RTOGS MA MYONG BA'I SO SO SKYE BO RNAMS LA, GZUGS SOGS KYI CHOS RNAMS BDEN GRUB TU SNANG BA DANG ZHEN PA GNYIS KA YOD, DAG SA LA GNAS PA'I BYANG SEMS RNAMS KYI RJES THOB KYI NGOR CHOS RNAMS BDEN GRUB TU SNANG BA YOD KYANG ZHEN PA MED DE, GNAS LUGS MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I SLOB PA 'PHAGS PA RNAMS LA, GZUGS SOGS KYI CHOS RNAMS LA BDEN GRUB KYI SNANG ZHEN GNYIS KA MED PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: sgyu ma mkhan gyis rde shing rta glang du sprul ba'i tshe, sngags rdzas kyis mig bslad pa'i ltad mo ba rnams la rde shing rta glang du snang ba dang zhen pa gnyis yod, sgyu ma mkhan rang nyid la rta glang du snang ba tsam yod kyang , zhen pa med sngags rdzas kyis mig ma bslad pa'i phyis kyi ltad mo ba la rde shing rta glang du snang zhen gnyis ka med pa de bzhin du gzugs sogs kyi chos rnams kyi steng du snang zhen mi 'dra ba gsum 'byung ste, stong nyid rtogs ma myong ba'i so so skye bo rnams la, gzugs sogs kyi chos rnams bden grub tu snang ba dang zhen pa gnyis ka yod, dag sa la gnas pa'i byang sems rnams kyi rjes thob kyi ngor chos rnams bden grub tu snang ba yod kyang zhen pa med de, gnas lugs mngon sum du rtogs pa'i slob pa 'phags pa rnams la, gzugs sogs kyi chos rnams la bden grub kyi snang zhen gnyis ka med pa'i phyir
rows.english: Suppose a magician makes a little piece of wood appear as a horse or cow. Spectators whose eyes have been affected by his spell both see the piece of wood as a horse or cow and believe that it really is. The magician himself only sees the horse or cow; he has no belief that it is real. A spectator who arrives later, who hasn't had the spell cast on him, neither sees the piece of wood as a horse or cow nor believes that it is. Three different combinations of seeing and believing exist as well with physical form and other such phenomena. The kind of people we call "common" people, those who have never had a realization of emptiness, both see and believe that form and the rest really exist. Bodhisattvas who are at one of the pure levels see phenomena as really existing during the periods following emptiness meditation; but they do not believe it. Realized beings who are not yet Buddhas, and who are in the state where they are realizing the way things are directly, neither see physical form and other such phenomena as really existing, nor do they believe that they really exist. 28 Difference between the Two Middle-Way Groups

rows.english: Here is the second part [of a different] discussion [about where the Madhyamika school believes the mental seeds from karma are planted, since they do not accept the concept of foundation consciousness]. One may begin with the following question: Suppose you deny then the existence of a foundation consciousness. Nonetheless you must accept that mental seeds from virtue or non-virtue do get planted, and that consequences do arise from the ripening of these mental seeds. After all, the autocommentary to Entering the Middle Way does state that "For time without beginning, in the suffering cycle of life, the mental seeds for things have been planted, and have then ripened, and have then been interpreted by people as the things themselves." There are as well many other quotations which mention the same thing. And it would be incorrect to say that there existed no basis or place where these mental seeds were planted. What then, according to your view, provides this place for the seeds to be planted?

rows.english: For what reason is it so? Because long ago there was a time, o Subhuti, when the king of Kalingka got the evil suspicion that I had engaged in relations with his woman. And so he was cutting off the larger limbs, and smaller appendages of my body. (The latter refers to the fingers and toes.) At that moment I practiced patience, keeping my mind on an understanding of the lack of true existence to each of the three elements to the act of patience. As I focussed on the "me" which exists nominally, there came into my mind no conception where I held any belief in some truly existing "me": and so I had no conception of anything from a truly existing "self" up to a truly existing "person." At that moment I had no conception at all of any such conception that something was existing truly. At the same time though it was neither as if I had no other, nominal conceptions at all. What Subhuti is saying here is the following. I did have the thought that I would have to keep my patience: I did have the thought to take the pain on willingly, and not to be upset about the harm being done to me. And I did have the kind of conception where I reconfirmed my knowledge of how I had perceived that no existing object has any true existence.
rows.raw: {"course": "C17", "acip": "RGYU MTSAN NI RAB 'BYOR SNGON GYI DUS GANG GI TSE KA LING KA'I RGYAL POS NGA KHO RANG GI BUD MED DANG 'BREL LAM SNYAM PA'I DOGS NGAN BYUNG STE RAL GRIS NGA'I YAN LAG DANG NYING LAG SOR MO RNAMS BCAD PAR GYUR PA DE'I TSE, NGAS BZOD PA'I 'KHOR GSUM BDEN MED DU SHES NAS BZOD PA BSGOMS PAS, THA SNYAD PA'I NGA LA DMIGS NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU BDAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES NAS GANG ZAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES KYANG MA BYUNG ZHING , DE'I TSE NGA LA DE LTA BU'I BDEN ZHEN GYI 'DU SHES CI YANG MED LA, THA SNYAD DU 'DU SHES GZHAN MED PAR GYUR PA YANG MA YIN TE, BZOD DO SNYAM PA'I SDUG BSNGAL DANG LEN DANG GNOD PA LA JI MI SNYAM PA DANG , BDEN MED DU RTOGS PA'I CHOS LA NGES SEMS KYI 'DU SHES RNAMS YOD PA'I PHYIR RO SNYAM DU DGONGS SO,", "wylie": "rgyu mtshan ni rab 'byor sngon gyi dus gang gi tshe ka ling ka'i rgyal pos nga kho rang gi bud med dang 'brel lam snyam pa'i dogs ngan byung ste ral gris nga'i yan lag dang nying lag sor mo rnams bcad par gyur pa de'i tshe, ngas bzod pa'i 'khor gsum bden med du shes nas bzod pa bsgoms pas, tha snyad pa'i nga la dmigs nas nga'o snyam du bdag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes nas gang zag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes kyang ma byung zhing , de'i tshe nga la de lta bu'i bden zhen gyi 'du shes ci yang med la, tha snyad du 'du shes gzhan med par gyur pa yang ma yin te, bzod do snyam pa'i sdug bsngal dang len dang gnod pa la ji mi snyam pa dang , bden med du rtogs pa'i chos la nges sems kyi 'du shes rnams yod pa'i phyir ro snyam du dgongs so", "english": "For what reason is it so? Because long ago there was a time, o Subhuti, when the king of Kalingka got the evil suspicion that I had engaged in relations with his woman. And so he was cutting off the larger limbs, and smaller appendages of my body. (The latter refers to the fingers and toes.) At that moment I practiced patience, keeping my mind on an understanding of the lack of true existence to each of the three elements to the act of patience. As I focussed on the \"me\" which exists nominally, there came into my mind no conception where I held any belief in some truly existing \"me\": and so I had no conception of anything from a truly existing \"self\" up to a truly existing \"person.\" At that moment I had no conception at all of any such conception that something was existing truly. At the same time though it was neither as if I had no other, nominal conceptions at all. What Subhuti is saying here is the following. I did have the thought that I would have to keep my patience: I did have the thought to take the pain on willingly, and not to be upset about the harm being done to me. And I did have the kind of conception where I reconfirmed my knowledge of how I had perceived that no existing object has any true existence."}

rows.acip: ZHES PAS STON LA, DON NI, GZHAN GYI LAD MO DANG G-YAM LA RGYUG TZAM MA YIN PAR 'KHOR BA MTHA' DAG LA ZHEN PA GTING NAS LOG STE YID NGES PAR 'BYUNG BA'I BSAM PAS RGYU BYAS PA STE KUN NAS BSLANGS TE, BLA MA'I SPYAN SNGAR GZHAN LA GNOD PA LUS NGAG GI MI DGE BA BDUN DANG , BDUN PO DE'I GZHI YID KYI MI DGE BA GSUM MAM BCAS PA'I KHA NA MA THO BA DANG BCAS PA LAS LDOG PAR KHAS BLANGS SHING DAM BCAS PA'I SDOM PA DE SO THAR GYI SDOM PA'I NGO BO'I ZHES PA'O,
rows.wylie: zhes pas ston la, don ni, gzhan gyi lad mo dang g-yam la rgyug tsam ma yin par 'khor ba mtha' dag la zhen pa gting nas log ste yid nges par 'byung ba'i bsam pas rgyu byas pa ste kun nas bslangs te, bla ma'i spyan sngar gzhan la gnod pa lus ngag gi mi dge ba bdun dang , bdun po de'i gzhi yid kyi mi dge ba gsum mam bcas pa'i kha na ma tho ba dang bcas pa las ldog par khas blangs shing dam bcas pa'i sdom pa de so thar gyi sdom pa'i ngo bo'i zhes pa'o
rows.english: Here Je Tsongkapa is saying that one's commitment to these vows should be caused by--that is, motivated by--an attitude where one feels a deep disgust for every single inch of the cycle of suffering life, and has thus decided to renounce it. You should not take the vows simply because you are imitating someone else, or just following the crowd. The basic nature of the vows then is as follows. In the presence of your Lama, you agree and pledge yourself to turn away from harming others; you agree to refrain from the seven physical and verbal deeds which are wrong by nature, and to avoid their basis as well. Here the word "basis" refers either to the three mental bad deeds that act as a foundation for the seven, or else to those bad deeds which were prohibited by Lord Buddha. 5 The Different Types of Vows

rows.wylie: dang po ni, spang bar 'os pa de lta bas na nyon mongs gzhom pa la dus rtag tu bsam sbyor gang yang phyir mi ldog par bya'o, , nyon mongs kyi gnyen po 'di la bdag gis zhen pa ste ched du bsten par bya zhing nyon mongs la khon du gzung nas g-yul bskrad la gzhom par bya'o
rows.english: Here is the first of the two. The mental afflictions are, therefore, things which deserve to be eliminated. As such, I should never turn back, either in my thoughts or my actions, from the task of destroying them, even for a single moment. I should get attached to these antidotes for the mental afflictions; that is, I should make use of the antidotes. And I should learn to hate the mental afflictions, and make war on them, and smash them.

rows.acip: ,SPANG GNYEN LA CHAGS SDANG DANG SPANG BYA LA KHON DU 'DZIN PA NYID NYON MONGS YIN PAS SPANG BYAR 'GYUR RO ZHE NA, GNYEN PO LA ZHEN PA DANG SPANG BYA LA KHON DU 'DZIN PA RNAM PA DE 'DRA'I NYON MONGS PA LTAR SNANG BA NI NYON MONGS 'JOMS PAR BYED PA'I GNYEN PO'I PHYOGS YIN PAS SPANG BYAR MA GTOGS SO, , 'GREL PAR PHYIS DE YANG GZHOM BYAR BSHAD PA NI SPANG BYA ZAD PA NA SPANG GNYEN G-YUL SPROD MI DGOS PA'I DON TO,
rows.wylie: spang gnyen la chags sdang dang spang bya la khon du 'dzin pa nyid nyon mongs yin pas spang byar 'gyur ro zhe na, gnyen po la zhen pa dang spang bya la khon du 'dzin pa rnam pa de 'dra'i nyon mongs pa ltar snang ba ni nyon mongs 'joms par byed pa'i gnyen po'i phyogs yin pas spang byar ma gtogs so, , 'grel par phyis de yang gzhom byar bshad pa ni spang bya zad pa na spang gnyen g-yul sprod mi dgos pa'i don to
rows.english: Someone may ask the following question: "You seem to be describing some kind of bias in the attitude we should have towards the antidotes that eliminate our mental afflictions, and you have spoken about hating the thing that the antidote is supposed to eliminate. Aren't these types of thoughts themselves just another kind of mental affliction--that is, the very thing which we are trying to eliminate?" These kinds of attitudes--of being attached to the antidotes for mental affliction, and of hating the mental afflictions we are trying to eliminate--are themselves only apparent mental afflictions. Because they are included into the antidote side--that is, because they are part of what acts to destroy the mental afflictions--they are not counted among the objects which we seek to eliminate from our minds. There are commentaries which do state that these are themselves something to be destroyed later, but what they mean by saying this is that, once one has finished off all the objects to be eliminated, one need no longer make war. 8 The Power of Resolve

rows.english: Here next I will explain the things that work against "it"--meaning effort. What exactly are they? First there is laziness, which is feeling attracted to the pleasant feeling of sloth, a condition where the mind and body become unfit to function well. rows.wylie: byang chub sems dpa' snying rje'i bsam pa dag pa des lus gtong ba la lus kyi sdug bsngal med de, sgo gsum gyi sdig pa mtha' dag spangs pa'i phyir lus gtong ba'i dus la mkhas pa'i phyir na yid la mi dga' ba yang med la, rgyu mtshan 'di ltar gang zag gi bdag dang bdag gir zhen pa'i log par rtog pa dang , srog gcod sogs sdig pa'i sems dang lus la gnod pa yin gyi sems dpa' chen po rnams la gnod pa'i rgyu log pas so
rows.english: Bodhisattvas who have reached the point where their thoughts of compassion are completely pure feel no pain in their bodies when they give them away. This is the case since they have stopped each and every kind of bad deed. Neither when they give their bodies away is there any kind of dislike for the act, because they are wise in knowing when it is right for them to do so. This is due to the fact--this is caused by the reason--that thinking of things the wrong way (believing that a person or the things which belong to a person could ever have any self-nature), along with doing negative deeds such as taking life and the rest, harm the body and mind; and great bodhisattvas have managed to stop these sources of harm. Contemplation Fourteen The use of power

rows.acip: GZHAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS BDAG LA MI GNOD PA RANG GI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS GZHAN LA MI GNOD PA DANG 'DRA BAS, DE CHED DU SEL BA RANG GI SDUG BSNGAL SEL BA DANG MTSUNGS PA MI 'THAD DO ZHE NA, SKYON MED DE, GZHAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS RANG LA MI GNOD PA LTAR, GAL TE BDAG GI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS GZHAN GYI LUS LA MI GNOD PA DE LTA NA'ANG DE BDAG GI SDUG BSNGAL YIN TE, RANG LA BDAG TU ZHEN PAS RANG GI SDUG BSNGAL MI BZOD PA 'BYUNG BA NYID YIN PA DE BZHIN DU SEMS CAN GZHAN YANG BDAG TU GZUNG BA GOMS PAS GZHAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL DAG BDAG LA 'BAB PAR MI 'GYUR YANG , DE LTA NA'ANG SEMS CAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL DE BDAG GIS BSAL BAR BYA BA'I SDUG BSNGAL YIN TE, SEMS CAN LA RANG GIS BDAG TU ZHEN PAS DE LA SDUG BSNGAL BYUNG NA BZOD PAR DKA' BAR 'GYUR RO,
rows.wylie: gzhan gyi sdug bsngal gyis bdag la mi gnod pa rang gi sdug bsngal gyis gzhan la mi gnod pa dang 'dra bas, de ched du sel ba rang gi sdug bsngal sel ba dang mtshungs pa mi 'thad do zhe na, skyon med de, gzhan gyi sdug bsngal gyis rang la mi gnod pa ltar, gal te bdag gi sdug bsngal gyis gzhan gyi lus la mi gnod pa de lta na'ang de bdag gi sdug bsngal yin te, rang la bdag tu zhen pas rang gi sdug bsngal mi bzod pa 'byung ba nyid yin pa de bzhin du sems can gzhan yang bdag tu gzung ba goms pas gzhan gyi sdug bsngal dag bdag la 'bab par mi 'gyur yang , de lta na'ang sems can gyi sdug bsngal de bdag gis bsal bar bya ba'i sdug bsngal yin te, sems can la rang gis bdag tu zhen pas de la sdug bsngal byung na bzod par dka' bar 'gyur ro
rows.english: One may make yet another objection: Two facts here are the same: the pain that others have doesn't hurt me; and the pain that I have doesn't hurt others. Therefore you are incorrect when you say that I should make very intentional efforts to remove their pain in exactly the same way that I make efforts to remove my own pain. Yet there is no such problem in our reasoning. Suppose you do object this way, and say that your pain never hurts the body of another, any more than their pain hurts you. Even so, their pain is your pain. This is because your own pain is something you find unbearable for just one reason: your habit of grasping to yourself as yourself. Suppose that, just so, you become accustomed to considering others yourself as well. Even though it may be true then that the sufferings which others feel may never come and strike you personally, still the suffering that these living beings feel is your suffering to work to remove, since you'll find it hard to bear it when sufferings come to them, once you have learned to grasp to them as being yourself. Contemplation Thirteen Logical proofs for compassion and love

rows.acip: ,STONG NYID MA RTOGS PA'I GANG ZAG DE DAG LA TSOR BA BDEN 'DZIN GYI MA RIG PA CUNG ZAD KYANG MA SPANGS PAS TSOR BA'I RKYEN GYIS TSOR BA BDE BA LA MI 'BRAL BAR SRED PA DANG , SDUG BSNGAL LA 'BRAL 'DOD KYI SRED PA NGES PAR SKYE BA YIN LA TSOR BA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR ZHEN PA KHYOD DGRA BCOM DU 'DOD PA DE DAG LA YOD PA'I PHYIR DNGOS PO LA BDEN PAR DMIGS PA DANG NI BCAS PA'I SEMS GANG ZAG 'GA' ZHIG GI RGYUD LA NI MNGON GYUR DU GNAS PAR 'GYUR BA DE SRID DU DES DRANGS PA'I SRED PA MNGON GYUR YANG LDOG PA MI SRID DO,
rows.wylie: stong nyid ma rtogs pa'i gang zag de dag la tshor ba bden 'dzin gyi ma rig pa cung zad kyang ma spangs pas tshor ba'i rkyen gyis tshor ba bde ba la mi 'bral bar sred pa dang , sdug bsngal la 'bral 'dod kyi sred pa nges par skye ba yin la tshor ba rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par zhen pa khyod dgra bcom du 'dod pa de dag la yod pa'i phyir dngos po la bden par dmigs pa dang ni bcas pa'i sems gang zag 'ga' zhig gi rgyud la ni mngon gyur du gnas par 'gyur ba de srid du des drangs pa'i sred pa mngon gyur yang ldog pa mi srid do
rows.english: People who have not yet realized emptiness have failed to eliminate even the slightest bit of that ignorance which consists of grasping to the true existence of their feelings. As such, there will definitely grow within them the kinds of craving brought about by their feelings; that is, the craving not to be separated from feelings of pleasure, and the craving to be separated from feelings of pain. Now those kinds of people that you say are enemy destroyers still though possess the belief that feelings can exist by definition. But the fact is that--so long as there remains in the continuum of any particular person a manifest form of the state of mind which still possesses the tendency to look at things as if they were true--then it is totally impossible that this person could have put a stop to the manifest form of the craving which is instigated by this tendency. Contemplation Fourteen On Emptiness and Nirvana Alone

rows.wylie: gal te bdag 'ga' rang bzhin gyis grub pa yod na ni der zhen pa las yul ci yang rung ba las 'jigs pa skye rigs par 'gyur na bdag nyid 'ga' yang rang bzhin gyis grub pa cung zad kyang yod pa min pas 'jigs par 'gyur ba po de su zhig yin te, rang bzhin sems pa'i blos kha nang du log la soms shig dang bdag med pa khong du chud pas 'jigs pa mtha' dag las grol bar 'gyur ba yin no
rows.english: Only if it were true that there were any self-nature of anything at all then would it be right for you to feel fear towards any object at all, since this fear comes from believing in a self-nature. But since it is not the case that anything has any nature at all which exists by nature, how could there be anyone who is afraid in the first place? Take this state of mind where you think that things have any nature of their own, and turn it around: look inside, and think! You will come to comprehend fully what it means when we say that nothing is itself at all, and you will liberate yourself from every fear there could ever be. Contemplation Sixteen The Two Kinds of Grasping to Self-Existence

rows.english: The point here is the same as in places where, for example, it's stated that the physical body is not the self. As such, the things focused upon for the two objects that are pictured in the mind during the innate form of the view of destruction are the simple "me" which serves as the basis for the workings of karma and its consequences, as well as the simple thing which is delineated as "mine." The view of destruction focuses upon these things and believes them to be a "me" and "mine" which exist by definition. Given all this, then if the "me" were to exist by definition, it would also be true that the collection of the heaps, and their continued existence, and all its components and parts, and anything completely separate from these things at all, any of them, would have to constitute what "me" refers to. The fact though is that none of these things constitutes anything of the kind. This is what is being expressed at this point.

rows.acip: 'KHOR BA'I SDUG BSNGAL LAS GROL BA'I RGYUR SMON PA NI BDAG NAM ZHIG CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG BAR RTOGS PA DMIGS PA MED PA'I SHES RAB DANG LDAN PA'I TSUL DU GUS PAR DE'I THABS SBYIN PA LA SOGS PA'I BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS MTHA' YAS PA BSAGS TE BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I DMIGS PAS 'KHOR BAR PHUNG BAR 'GYUR BA'I SEMS CAN RNAMS LA 'KHOR BA'I SDUG BSNGAL ZHI BA'I CHED DU STONG PA NYID NI STON PAR 'GYUR SNYAM NAS SEMS CAN RNAMS 'KHOR BA'I SDUG BSNGAL DANG BRAL NA, BRAL BA DE BDAG GIS BYA'O SNYAM PA'I SNYING RJE CHEN PO BSGOM PAR BYA'O,
rows.wylie: 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal las grol ba'i rgyur smon pa ni bdag nam zhig chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis stong bar rtogs pa dmigs pa med pa'i shes rab dang ldan pa'i tshul du gus par de'i thabs sbyin pa la sogs pa'i bsod nams kyi tshogs mtha' yas pa bsags te bden par zhen pa'i dmigs pas 'khor bar phung bar 'gyur ba'i sems can rnams la 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal zhi ba'i ched du stong pa nyid ni ston par 'gyur snyam nas sems can rnams 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal dang bral na, bral ba de bdag gis bya'o snyam pa'i snying rje chen po bsgom par bya'o
rows.english: Here is a prayer that we become the cause for their liberation from suffering: When is it that I will come to realize that every single object which exists is completely devoid of any nature of its own? When will I come to have the wisdom that has no focus [towards things as self- existent]? And when will I, with great respect, go about the task of accumulating infinite masses of merit, acts of giving and the rest, using this wisdom as a method to achieve the goals? Living beings are all devastated here in the cycle of suffering by their tendency to focus on things and believe that they have some true existence. When is it that I will be able to teach them the concept of emptiness, in order to help them put a stop to all the sufferings of the cycle? Meditate thus on great compassion, think to yourself: What if it were true that every living being could be freed from the sufferings of this cycle of life? May I free them myself!

rows.english: There's no way you can do without Living the ethical life. But if you do so Because you're attached to goals of this life, Then you've planted the roots for living in The eight worldly thoughts. You'll disparage those whose ethics are less. You'll feel jealous of those who keep Their ethics well. The ethics you follow yourself Will be done for the recognition of others. You will plant the seeds for the lower realms. You will slip into being a person Whose ethical life is a sham.

rows.english: There's no way you can do without Learning and contemplation. But a person Whose learning and contemplation are done Attached to worldly kinds of goals Is only gaining the resources which Will allow them to reach the state of pride. They will speak badly of those whose learning And contemplation are less than theirs. They will be jealous of others Whose learning and contemplation are good. The people around them, and all they own, Will never be very stable. They are planting roots to grow As a birth in the lower realms. They have slipped into learning and contemplation That is lost to the eight worldly thoughts.

rows.english: Think of the universal pain. The things you have to do Will never end. It hurts to be around many people, And it hurts to be around few. It hurts to have money, And it hurts to be hungry. Everyone alive is standing in line, And the line moves to the final end. When they reach the front of the line, Everybody dies. But the lines don't end there. You join the back of the line In the next realm you must go. Pity the man or woman Who feels any attachment To the mind and body of a being In this vicious circle of pain.

rows.acip: NGO BO NYID MED PAR GSUNGS PA'I NGO BO NYID MED TSUL NI DE LTAR DU BSHAD KYI DE LTA MIN PAR NGO BO NYID GSUM GA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MA GRUB PA LA NGO BO NYID MED PAR BSHAD NA NGO BO NYID MED PAR GSUNGS PA'I MDO SDE LA SGRA JI BZHIN PAR ZHEN PA YIN LA, DE LTA NA MED LTA'AM CHAD PAR LTA BA THOB PAR 'GYUR TE NGO BO NYID GSUM GA LA SKUR BA 'DEBS PAS MTSAN NYID MED PAR LTA BA CAN DU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO, ,
rows.wylie: ngo bo nyid med par gsungs pa'i ngo bo nyid med tshul ni de ltar du bshad kyi de lta min par ngo bo nyid gsum ga rang gi mtshan nyid kyis ma grub pa la ngo bo nyid med par bshad na ngo bo nyid med par gsungs pa'i mdo sde la sgra ji bzhin par zhen pa yin la, de lta na med lta'am chad par lta ba thob par 'gyur te ngo bo nyid gsum ga la skur ba 'debs pas mtshan nyid med par lta ba can du 'gyur ba'i phyir ro,
rows.english: This is the way one should explain how it is that things lack any nature of their own when the sutra speaks of a "lack of any nature of their own." If on the other hand one were to say that "lacking any nature of their own" meant that none of the three natures existed by definition, then you would be expressing the belief that the sutras which state that nothing has any nature of its own are to be taken to mean exactly what they say. This would amount to espousing the view that nothing exists, or the view that everything has discontinued. This in turn would be discounting the existence of all three of the natures; and we could say then that you had turned into one of those people who holds the view that nothing has any definitive characteristics at all.

rows.english: In this same vein, the Commentary on the True Intent says: I will explain to you my true intent. It may be the case that you believe in things, that you fail to grasp fully the profound and pure way that things really are. And then you will come to believe, firmly, that I only meant exactly what I said about the nature of all things when I said the following: None of these things at all has any nature of its own; and they are no other way. None of these things at all ever grows; and they are no other way. None of them ever stops; and they are no other way. They are extinct, and have been so from the very beginning; and they are no other way. They have, by their very nature, gone completely beyond the state of grief; and they are no other way.

rows.acip: ,BYIS PA RGAS PA'I RGAN PO DE, ,SKYES TZAM NYID NAS RGAN PO RANG, ,GRUB GRUB 'DRA BA'I SNANG BA DANG, ,DE LA ZHEN PA NYID DANG MTSUNGS,
rows.wylie: byis pa rgas pa'i rgan po de, ,skyes tsam nyid nas rgan po rang, ,grub grub 'dra ba'i snang ba dang, ,de la zhen pa nyid dang mtshungs
rows.english: An old man is a boy grown old; But a boy who was old in actual fact From the moment he was born; And yet it seems to us That he grows old gradually. The way we believe now the world is real Is exactly the same as how we believe That the boy is how he appears to be. What really happens as we pass through a doorway?  A picture of a smaller doorway flies out; then a picture of a larger doorway as we pass through it; and then a final picture of another smaller doorway as we walk on to where the door leads. Aging is the same.  An avoidable tragedy.

rows.english: Where this one thing Stands complete— Where we misunderstand our world— The cycle of pain continues on, The cycle never-ending. And in it we each are born Into each of the five different Forms of life; And in each individual life We look upon Each body and mind And hold them to exist in truth. It seems as though The way you grasp to things— As depending on nothing else at all, As relying on nothing else there is— Is as well itself a belief That will have to be immutable! How we view our body and mind—in each lifetime we live—forces us to enter more & more bodies and minds of the same kind: suffering.  The cycle of these lifetimes is here described as “never-ending”; but this only applies when we are still misunderstanding where everything around us comes from. There will come a day—soon, if we work to understand the lines of The Cantos—that this otherwise never-ending cycle of pain will finally and perfectly end. rows.acip: ,SNANG NGO'I BDEN SNANG GTAN LOG PAS, ,DE GNYIS SRANG MDA' MTHO DMAN BZHIN, ,ZHEN PA'ANG DE BZHIN MTSUNGS PA YIN,
rows.wylie: snang ngo'i bden snang gtan log pas, ,de gnyis srang mda' mtho dman bzhin, ,zhen pa'ang de bzhin mtshungs pa yin
rows.english: At this point we will have Stopped, entirely, The appearance to Our perceptions that Things could ever be real. With that then these two Swing the other way, Moving like the dishes Of a scale, one descending As the other begins to rise. And our belief In this appearance Will follow just the same. It's perhaps valuable to consider the question of whether there is any natural connection between seeing things as "real" (in the sense of coming from their own side) and our human tendency not to feel that the people and events swirling around us might possess some divine purpose, meant for our ultimate benefit. What His Holiness is saying here is that it is the very nature of things that when one dish of a scale descends, the other dish automatically rises.  The more our tendency to see things as coming from their own side asserts itself, the more likely we are to take life as "normal"; the more we understand how everything is actually coming from our own mental seeds, the more likely we are to see ourselves living in a divine world.

rows.english: At this point, here is how you should be thinking: For time with no beginning, the mind itself has been attached to a mistaken idea about physical forms and the like. rows.english: And what will this ascertainment do for us?  We would have to say, first of all, that it is not the case that we would be able then to reject the attraction we feel with our sense perception—with the state of mind holding to blue, the state of mind which has taken on a subject aspect—as it grasps to the blue and is strongly attracted to the idea that it exists in reality. rows.english: Here then is how we express the meaning of the statement here, in a syllogism: Let us consider the state of mind where we ascertain—through a reason which helps us ascertain that they are perceived together—the fact that the blue does not consist of any substance separate from the sense awareness which has taken on an aspect of the blue. The third level of deep practice

rows.wylie: dang po ni, ngar 'dzin gyi 'jig ltas nga yir 'dzin pa'i 'jig lta skyed pas, sems can 'di rnams ni dang por te bdag gi bar mngon par zhen pa'i 'jig lta'i snga rol tu, ngar 'dzin pa'i 'jig ltas rang bzhin gyis yod pa min pa'i bdag rang bzhin gyis yod do snyam nas, nga zhes pa'i don 'di nyid du ste la bden par mngon par zhen par byed do
rows.english: We begin with the first. The version of the view of destruction where we hold to a “me” triggers the version where we hold to some “mine.” Thus all suffering beings first (that is, before they give rise to the view of destruction where they begin wanting what is “mine”) give rise to the view of destruction where they want a “me,” talking about something which is a thing that is itself—which exists “in reality.” This is a view of “me” which thinks to itself that a person who could never exist in & of themselves does exist in & of themselves.

rows.wylie: 'dis ni gdags gzhi phung po la bden par zhen pa'i zhen yul sun ma phyin na, btags chos gang zag la bden par 'dzin pa'i zhen yul yang sun mi phyin pas, gang zag bden med du ma rtogs pa'i phyir, gang zag gi bdag med mtshan nyid rdzogs pa ma rtogs par bstan no
rows.english: What's being said here is that—if we are not able to use this realization to rip out the object that the belief in the thing we label ourselves (the parts of us) believes is real—then we will fail, in turn, to rip out the object that our tendency to think that things are real believes is real when it focuses on the result of the labeling: the person themselves. And then we will fail to realize that the person has no reality; and then we will fail to reach a realization which is complete in every respect as it sees that the person is not themselves.

rows.english: And so the Holy One is requesting an explanation of what object a person needs to focus upon—and in what way—in order to fail to free themselves from the cycle of suffering. rows.english: What does it mean then when we say that a person has “rid oneself of a belief in objects of the mind—outer objects”? rows.english: As for this expression, “sphere of reality,” we see it explained in the Illumination of the Twenty Thousand: When we talk about “thinking that something is there” or “imagining that something is there,” we're referring to a belief in things, and the indicators of things. The ultimate nature of things is in fact nothing other than this same quality, of not even existing.

rows.english: This brings us to our third point from above: a description of what it is we rid ourselves of at the fourth level. And then everything related to seeing things as themselves is finished off completely—which is to say, everything related to seeing things as themselves as we do this in the subtle form of the view of destruction. This involves the tendency to believe in a self-nature which is the precursor for this view; the tendency to believe in the gross form of a self-nature to a person in the case where we are holding living beings & such as existing in a self-standing, substantial way (in addition to thinking this way about what is possessed by such a being); and the tendency to believe in a self-nature to the parts of a person: the heaps, the categories, & the doors of sense—thinking that these are real.

rows.acip: 'O NA BDAG GI 'DI ZHES ZHES PA'I RANG 'GREL LAS, 'DI NI BDAG GI'O SNYAM DU NGAR 'DZIN PA'I YUL LAS GZHAN PA'I DNGOS PO'I RNAM PA MA LUS PA LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA YIN NO, ZHES MIG LA SOGS PA'I GZHI LA DMIGS NAS 'DI NI BDAG GI YIN NO SNYAM DU ZHEN PA BDAG GIR 'DZIN PAR BSHAD PA JI LTAR YIN SNYAM NA,

rows.english: The following question might then arise in ones mind: Now then; at the point where it mentions “We say of them 'mine',” the autocommentary also states that “when we say 'mine,' we hold a false belief in all entities other than the object we hold when we say 'me'.” What about this particular reference, which seems to be saying that when we focus on objects such as the eye and believe in them, wrongly—thinking that “this is mine”—then this is the tendency to hold things as “mine”?

rows.wylie: de ni mig sogs rnams bdag gi bar mthong nas bdag gi ba la bden par mngon par zhen pa'i don yin gyi, bdag gi ba'i mtshan gzhi mig sogs dmigs par ston pa min te, de ltar ma yin na 'jig lta dang chos kyi bdag 'dzin gnyis mi 'gal bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
rows.english: The point of this reference though is to say that we see the eye and so on as being something of mine, and then hold the false belief that it is something of mine in a real sense. This is not though meant to indicate that we are directing our perceptions towards the eye and so on as a classical example of the concept of “mine.” If this were not the case, then the two of the view of destruction and the tendency to believe in a self-nature of things would no longer be mutually exclusive.

rows.acip: CI STE YANG DE LTAR DNGOS PO LA BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA THAMS CAD GCOD PA NA, BRED SHA 'THON PA THA SNYAD KYI BDEN PA LA BDEN PAR ZHEN PA 'DI GANG KUN BYANG GNYIS KYI 'CHING GROL GYI RGYUR 'GYUR BA, RDZAS TE RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I BDAG NYID 'GA' ZHIG TU SKYE BAR 'GYUR BA CIG BYA DGOS SO ZHES SMRA NA, DE SKAD DU SMRA BA LA NI TSIG TZAM ZHIG LHAG MAR LUS PAR 'GYUR RO,,
rows.wylie: ci ste yang de ltar dngos po la bden par mngon par zhen pa thams cad gcod pa na, bred sha 'thon pa tha snyad kyi bden pa la bden par zhen pa 'di gang kun byang gnyis kyi 'ching grol gyi rgyur 'gyur ba, rdzas te rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i bdag nyid 'ga' zhig tu skye bar 'gyur ba cig bya dgos so zhes smra na, de skad du smra ba la ni tshig tsam zhig lhag mar lus par 'gyur ro
rows.english: Well now, how is it? Suppose that, as we've described it, people start to eliminate all of their tendencies to grasp to things existing in reality. Then though their faces take on a certain look of panic, and they start feeling a strong belief that nominal reality though must be real. That is, they begin to say that there must exist objects which act as causes behind the bondage and the liberation going on with the negative side of things, and the enlightened side of things. And they feel that these causes must be creating some number of entities which are substantial; that is, which exist by definition. But these kinds of proclamations end up just being all words, and nothing else.

rows.english: Even if we don't accept the idea of a foundation consciousness, we still have to agree that virtuous and non-virtuous deep seeds can be planted; and that as these seeds ripen, they give forth results. As the autocommentary to Entering the Middle Way puts it, In the cycle of suffering with no beginning, the deep seeds of things have been planted, and have ripened. And we have had a deep belief in those things… And we see many other such references as well.

rows.acip: DBU SEMS GANG GI LUGS KYIS KYANG DE LTA SEMS CAN RNAMS LA SNANG ZHING, SNANG BA LTAR DU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I ZHE NA {%ZHEN} GZHI DE, ZHEN YUL DES STONG PAR BSTAN PA CIG YOD NA, STONG NYID DE RTOGS PA LAM DU 'GRO BA YIN GYI,
rows.wylie: dbu sems gang gi lugs kyis kyang de lta sems can rnams la snang zhing, snang ba ltar du bden par zhen pa'i zhe na {%zhen} gzhi de, zhen yul des stong par bstan pa cig yod na, stong nyid de rtogs pa lam du 'gro ba yin gyi
rows.english: It doesn't matter which system we're talking about—that of the Middle Way, or that of the Mind Only. In either case, there is a basis behind our wrong belief: something that appears to living beings to exist in a certain way, and which they subsequently believe to exist in truth, as it appears to. If there is something that we can point to as being empty of the object that people believe they see, then—and only then—the realization of that sheer absence or emptiness can function as a path.

rows.acip: SEMS CAN RANG DGA' BA RNAMS KYIS BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I ZHEN YUL SUN PHYUNG BA'I STONG NYID RTOGS PA LAM DU MI BYED PAR STONG PA GZHAN CIG BDEN PAR SGRUB PA NI, THOG MA MED PA NAS ZHUGS PA'I BDEN ZHEN PHRA RAGS GANG GI YANG GNYEN POR MI 'GRO BAS NGAL BA 'BRAS MED DO,,
rows.wylie: sems can rang dga' ba rnams kyis bden par zhen pa'i zhen yul sun phyung ba'i stong nyid rtogs pa lam du mi byed par stong pa gzhan cig bden par sgrub pa ni, thog ma med pa nas zhugs pa'i bden zhen phra rags gang gi yang gnyen por mi 'gro bas ngal ba 'bras med do
rows.english: And suppose we fail to make a path out of coming to a realization of emptiness—an emptiness where we have overthrown that object of belief: the belief of just normal people of the world that things exist in reality. That is, suppose we take some other kind of emptiness to exist, really. This could never serve as an antidote for either one of the forms—more subtle, or more coarse—of the belief in something real which has resided in the hearts of beings for time with no beginning. And as such, the whole exercise would be one in futility.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS KYI SKYE MCHED MED PA KHO NA YIN ZHING, YID KYI RNAM PAR SHES PA LA PHYI ROL DE'I RNAM PA SNANG BA TZAM LA PHYI ROL NYID DU MNGON PAR ZHEN PA NI BZLOG TU MED PAR 'BYUNG NGO,,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir phyi rol gyi gzugs kyi skye mched med pa kho na yin zhing, yid kyi rnam par shes pa la phyi rol de'i rnam pa snang ba tsam la phyi rol nyid du mngon par zhen pa ni bzlog tu med par 'byung ngo
rows.english: As such, an outer door of visible form can only be something which does not exist. And what's happening is that we are strongly attached to thinking that the awareness of the thought is an aspect of the outer world—that something which is nothing more than the appearance of being outside is the outside world itself. This attachment occurs in a very compelling way that is difficult to reverse.

rows.acip: DES NA DBU SEMS SU YI LUGS LA YANG SEMS CAN RNAMS GANG LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA'I GZHI, PHYI NANG GI CHOS SU SNANG BA 'DI DAG LA BYED PA LA NI MI 'DRA BA MED LA, DE RNAMS STONG PAR STON PA NI GZHI DE LA MNGON ZHEN ZLOG PA'I PHYIR DU YIN PA YANG 'DRA MOD KYANG, ZHEN TSUL LA MI MTHUN TE
rows.wylie: des na dbu sems su yi lugs la yang sems can rnams gang la mngon par zhen pa'i gzhi, phyi nang gi chos su snang ba 'di dag la byed pa la ni mi 'dra ba med la, de rnams stong par ston pa ni gzhi de la mngon zhen zlog pa'i phyir du yin pa yang 'dra mod kyang, zhen tshul la mi mthun te
rows.english: Thus we can say that—whether we are speaking about the system of the Middle Way, or to that of the Mind Only—there is no difference in the fact that we are referring to the way that outer & inner entities make their appearance: we are speaking of that foundational state of things which living beings are holding on to. When we clarify that these things are empty, the statement in each of the two systems is similar in that we are attempting to put a stop to how people hold on to this foundation; and yet the way in which each system describes the holding on that people do is incompatible.

rows.acip: SEMS TZAM PAS NI GZUNG 'DZIN GNYIS PHYI NANG DU RGYANGS CHAD DU SNANG BA LA SNANG BA LTAR DU, GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS THA DAD DU ZHEN PA YIN LA, DE'I GNYEN POR SNANG BA GZHAN DBANG 'DI CHOS CAN DU BZUNG NAS, GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS THA DAD DU YOD PA 'GOG PA YIN PAS DGAG GZHI DE DGAG BYA DE YIN PA 'GOG PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: sems tsam pas ni gzung 'dzin gnyis phyi nang du rgyangs chad du snang ba la snang ba ltar du, gzung 'dzin rdzas tha dad du zhen pa yin la, de'i gnyen por snang ba gzhan dbang 'di chos can du bzung nas, gzung 'dzin rdzas tha dad du yod pa 'gog pa yin pas dgag gzhi de dgag bya de yin pa 'gog pa yin no
rows.english: That is, the Mind Only would say that the belief that people hold to here is that objects and their subjects are essentially separate, as they appear to be when it seems that—for the objects and subjects—those which are inside of us and those which are outside look to exist at a significant distance away from each other. And then as an antidote for this perception, we take what it is that appears—dominated entities—and take them as the subject under logical consideration, and then disprove that it could display any reality where objects & their subjects were essentially separate. Thus, the denial is done by taking this foundational state of things that we deny itself as the object we are denying, and work to deny that.

rows.wylie: dbu ma pa ltar na zhen tshul ni snang ba la tha snyad pa'i blos bzhag pa min pa'i bden grub tu zhen pa yin la, de'i gnyen por snang ba 'di chos can du bzung nas, de 'dra ba'i bden par med ces 'gog ste
rows.english: Those of the Middle Way describe the belief with which we hold to things in a different way. They say that we hold that things exist in reality—which is to say, we believe that what appears to us is not being established by a nominal state of mind. And then as an antidote for this belief, we start by taking this way that things appear to us as the subject under our logical consideration. Then we deny this appearance by saying, “This is not something which exists as real, in the way we have described that.”

rows.wylie: de yang dgag gzhi de dgag bya yin pa 'gog pa yin te, sems can gyis zhen pa na gzhi de la dgag bya de don gzhan du yod par 'dzin pa min par, gzhi de dgag bya de'i ngo bor zhen pa'i phyir dang, stong pa yang ji ltar zhen pa de ltar du yod pas stong par bstan dgos pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: This denial is a refusal that the objects which make up the foundation state where we are accomplishing our denial could in fact exist as what we are denying about them. This is not to say that when living beings are engaging in what they believe, they hold this foundation state to exist in some other way than that expressed by the object that we deny; rather, they actually hold that this state exists, in its very essence, as expressed by the object that we deny. Moreover, we have to demonstrate as well that emptiness itself is also empty of existing in the way that we might believe it to.

rows.wylie: shes bya dang shes pa la rang bzhin gyis yod med kyi khyad par med par ston pa yin la, skra shad med na der snang ba'i shes pa yang med ces pa dang, sgyu ma la rta glang du zhen pa'i zhen yul med na der 'dzin pa'i shes pa yang med ces sogs ni, slob dpon 'di'i lugs gtan min no
rows.english: What this is indicating is that there is no difference between knowable things and the awareness which knows them, as far as existing through some nature of their own, or not. And what this is saying is that—if there is no strand of hair—then neither is there any state of mind which is taking that strand as its aspect. It is absolutely not the position of this master though to say that—if the object that one was thinking was there when we perceived a horse or cow in an illusion didn't really exist—then the state of mind that was grasping to it didn't exist either.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR SEMS TZAM PA 'DI LA 'JIG RTEN GYI THA SNYAD KYI RGYU GANG YIN PA DE RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS YOD PA MIN PAS, KYE MA KYE HUD GZHAN SEMS TZAM PA'I LTAR NA NGES DON MTHAR THUG PA 'BYED PA'I SHES RAB KYI RTZAL MED PAS GZHAN DBANG GI RDZAS SHES TZAM LA BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I CHAGS PA YI SGO NAS, GZHAN DBANG GI BUM PA SO MA BTANG BAR,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir sems tsam pa 'di la 'jig rten gyi tha snyad kyi rgyu gang yin pa de rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis yod pa min pas, kye ma kye hud gzhan sems tsam pa'i ltar na nges don mthar thug pa 'byed pa'i shes rab kyi rtsal med pas gzhan dbang gi rdzas shes tsam la bden par zhen pa'i chags pa yi sgo nas, gzhan dbang gi bum pa so ma btang bar
rows.english: As such, let's consider these followers of the Mind Only. If it is the fact that what we say is that the cause in the parlance of the world is not something that could exist through any essential nature of its own, then oh my gosh! According to these other ones—the Mind Only (since they possess none of the fluency of wisdom which makes distinctions regarding the ultimate point of what was truly intended)—then dominated entities exist only as a mental substance, and are still real. These thinkers are attached to thinking of them thus, as real, and in this manner they approach a clay pot of the concept of dominated entities that was never properly fired.

rows.acip: DE LA DGONGS NAS GSUNGS PA'I DGOS PA NI BYIS PA RNAMS BDAG MED PAS 'JIGS PA SPANG BA DANG, MU STEGS BYED BDAG TU SMRA BA LA MNGON PAR ZHEN PA RNAMS DANG, SNGON DE'I LTA BA LA GOMS PAR BYAS PA RNAMS DE KHO NA NYID LA RIM GYIS DRANG BA'I PHYIR DU
rows.wylie: de la dgongs nas gsungs pa'i dgos pa ni byis pa rnams bdag med pas 'jigs pa spang ba dang, mu stegs byed bdag tu smra ba la mngon par zhen pa rnams dang, sngon de'i lta ba la goms par byas pa rnams de kho na nyid la rim gyis drang ba'i phyir du
rows.english: Why were these points then spoken of in terms of allusion? First of all, the Buddha wished to prevent any trepidation that the infants might feel towards the concept that things are not themselves. And he wanted to take those of the River Schools who were so attached to their profession of a self, and those who had, earlier, already accustomed themselves strongly to those ideas, and draw them out, gradually, to the idea of suchness.

rows.english: And so when we teach that there is a heart nature which is unchanging, stable, and solid, what we are really saying is that present and future bodhisattvas are not to feel any attachment to any self-nature here. And so the point is that we need to avoid doing this.

rows.acip: DE LTAR NA DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON GTAN LA PHAB PA GOMS PA LAS, RNAL 'BYOR PA 'PHAGS PA'I LAM MNGON SUM DU MDZAD PA'I MNYAM GZHAG GIS SNANG BA'I SPROS PA MA GZIGS PA'I TSUL GYIS DE KHO NA NYID GZIGS PA DE DAG LA CHOS GANG LA YANG BDEN PAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA'I RTOG PA THOG MA MED PA NAS GOMS PA RNAMS LDOG PAR 'GYUR TE,
rows.wylie: de ltar na de kho na nyid kyi don gtan la phab pa goms pa las, rnal 'byor pa 'phags pa'i lam mngon sum du mdzad pa'i mnyam gzhag gis snang ba'i spros pa ma gzigs pa'i tshul gyis de kho na nyid gzigs pa de dag la chos gang la yang bden par mngon par zhen pa'i rtog pa thog ma med pa nas goms pa rnams ldog par 'gyur te
rows.english: And so it is that when they have accustomed ourselves to establishing just what it is that suchness refers to, the deep practitioner is able to go into a balanced meditation where they can manifest—directly—the path of a realized being. And then this meditation helps them to see suchness, in the manner of not seeing the various ways that things might appear to one as false elaborations. Thus then are such people able to put a stop to any habit of the kind that we have possessed for time with no beginning, of a notion where they feel strongly attached to the idea that any object at all could exist in truth.

rows.acip: GAL TE DBU MA LA SEMS KYI RANG GI NGO BO'I BDAG NYID KYI DNGOS PO DON DAM PA CI YANG RUNG BA ZHIG YOD PAR GYUR NA NI, DE'I TSE DE LA YOD PAS RTAG GO ZHE'AM, MI RTAG GO ZHES BYA BAR MNGON PAR ZHEN PA YANG JI LTAR MTHAR 'GYUR TE, DNGOS PO'I DE KHO NA NYID JI LTA BA BZHIN GYI RJES SU SONG ZHING TSUL BZHIN YID LA BYED PA NYID NI, LTUNG BA'I GNAS SO ZHES BYA BAR RIGS PA MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PA BZHIN NO,,
rows.wylie: gal te dbu ma la sems kyi rang gi ngo bo'i bdag nyid kyi dngos po don dam pa ci yang rung ba zhig yod par gyur na ni, de'i tshe de la yod pas rtag go zhe'am, mi rtag go zhes bya bar mngon par zhen pa yang ji ltar mthar 'gyur te, dngos po'i de kho na nyid ji lta ba bzhin gyi rjes su song zhing tshul bzhin yid la byed pa nyid ni, ltung ba'i gnas so zhes bya bar rigs pa ma yin no, zhes gsungs pa bzhin no
rows.english: If it were the case that in the middle way there could ever be some kind of ultimately existing entity with some essential nature of its own, then at that point there could exist with that the deluded belief that “this is unchanging,” or “this is changing”; which is to say, there would be a way of holding to an extreme. That is, if a person has reached a place where they see the suchness of entities just as it really is, and if they are thinking of that in a perfectly correct manner, then it would never be appropriate to say of them, “They are at a place where they could fall.”

rows.english: One may wonder then just what kind of aspect it is that the view of destruction assumes, when it begins to hold its beliefs about any particular object. And what we come to realize is that what this view thinks it sees is what we have called “the self”—which is to say, a certain kind of “me.” It is the “me” which the view of some self thinks it is focused upon. And that is because the tendency to hold to “me” takes, as its object, a “self.”

rows.english: One may make yet another objection: Two facts here are the same: the pain that others have doesn't hurt me; and the pain that I have doesn't hurt others. Therefore you are incorrect when you say that I should make very intentional efforts to remove their pain in exactly the same way that I make efforts to remove my own pain. Yet there is no such problem in our reasoning. Suppose you do object this way, and say that your pain never hurts the body of another, any more than their pain hurts you. Even so, their pain is your pain. This is because your own pain is something you find unbearable for just one reason: your habit of grasping to yourself as yourself. Suppose that, just so, you become accustomed to consideringothers yourself as well. Even though it may be true then that the sufferings which others feel may never come and strike you personally, still the sufferingthat these livingbeings feel is your suffering to work to remove, since you'll find it hard to bear it when sufferings come to them, once you have learned to grasp to them as being Contemplation Five Logical proofs for compassion and love

rows.wylie: zer na ma khyab ste dang por yi dwags kyis chu ma mthong na phyogs der longs spyod, pa'i phyir 'gro ba yang mi 'thad pas dang por chu mthong yang phyis las kyi dbang, gis chu ma mthong bar 'og gzhi gram sreg tsam zhig mthong zhing de'i rjes su rtog, pas chu bskams par zhen pa dang de bzhin du dang por ljon shing gi 'bras bu mthong yang phyis las kyi dbang gis 'bras bu ma mthong bar yal ga tsam zhig mthong zhing de'i rjes su rtog pas 'bras bu med par zhen pa'i phyir
rows.english: Just because we said that about the other case doesn't mean that it's true in every case. If the craving spirit hadn't seen any water in that area in the first place, it wouldn't have made any sense for him to go over in that direction to try to enjoy some of the water. Therefore what happened was that, at first, he saw some water. Later on, he was forced by his karma to stop seeing water and saw only bare, parched earth. Then he had an impression where he thought the water had dried up. The case with the fruit tree is the same. Although at first the craving spirit sees a tree loaded with fruit, later on his karma forces him to stop seeing fruit, and all he sees is bare branches. Then he has an impression where he thinks that the tree has no fruit any more.

rows.english: Consider now bodhisattvas who have reached one of the pure levels. Even though objects appear to their minds, during what we call the "subsequent period," as something which exists truly, they have no belief in them this way. And this is because neither situation applies to realized beings who are not yet Buddhas and whoare perceiving the real nature of things directly; that is, physical matter and other objects do not appear to them as if they existed truly, and they do not believe that these objects exist that way.

rows.english: There are a number of expressions here. One is that “We should stay in our giving just as those who are striving in their giving.” Another is “We should try to practice in a way where we have no belief that the three spheres of this act are real.” And they are both to be explained as meaning “Maintain, perfectly, a state of mind where you are single-pointedly absorbed in the understanding that nothing is true.”

rows.english: And what Lord Buddha is saying then is: “O Subhuti, every single object in the universe exists only through our projections; they have not a single atom of any other kind of existence—any natural existence. rows.english: On this idea that—if we entertain some belief in a self where we say to ourselves, “This is me, ” we will begin as well to entertain thoughts of harming someone—the Commentary on Valid Perception states: Once there is a self, There is the idea of “other”; And then we hold tight To the “self” side And we feel dislike For the “other” side. Once we become enmeshed In these two different sides, Every other problem possible Then starts to come to us.

rows.english: If the One Thus Gone ever did entertain this state of mind, there would be the problem that he would be grasping to some self of the One Gone Thus, and to some living being, or to some person, or else to something that lives, of the One Gone Thus. And that would be wrong, for the fact is that the One Gone Thus doesn't have any of these thoughts—any of this grasping to a self, or to any of the rest. This is because he has given up each and every form of the belief where we grasp to some self.

rows.acip: MDOR NA, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA MING DANG GZUGS KYI SKUR BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PA DE DAG NI, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I CHOS KYI SKU LTA BA LA LOG PAR ZHUGS PA STE, SKYE BO DE DAG GIS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA NGA'I CHOS KYI SKU STONG PA NYID MI MTHONG NGO,,
rows.wylie: mdor na, de bzhin gshegs pa la ming dang gzugs kyi skur bden par zhen pa'i bden 'dzin gyis bcings pa de dag ni, de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi sku lta ba la log par zhugs pa ste, skye bo de dag gis de bzhin gshegs pa nga'i chos kyi sku stong pa nyid mi mthong ngo
rows.english: Which is to say—if we were to put it briefly—let us consider those who are shackled by the tendency to look upon the One Gone Thus and believe that he exists, in some real way, within either his name or his body of form. Such persons would be living in error as far as how they were viewing the reality body. People like this can't see me—that is, cannot see the reality body, or emptiness, that belongs to “me”: to the One Gone Thus.

rows.english: And this is precisely why, Lord Buddha says, that—nominally speaking—we can call it “gathering the merit in.” When the sutra says here that we are “not to gather,” it is helping us to avoid the view that things are unchanging—where we believe that the mountains of merit exist in truth. Reasoning for disproving that things could exist

rows.wylie: sbyin pa sbyin pa la brtson pa lta bu ni ji ltar gnas par bya zhes pa'i don dang, de'i 'khor gsum la bden par mi zhen pa ni ji ltar bsgrub par bya zhes pa'i don dang, bden med du rtogs pa'i blo la sems rtse gcig tu byed pa ni sems rab tu gzung bar bya zhes pa'i don du bshad de, phar phyin gzhan la'ang sbyar bar bya'o
rows.english: There are a number of expressions here. One is that "We should stay in our giving just as those who are striving in their giving." Another is "We should try to practice in a way where we have no belief that the three spheres of this act are real." And they are both to be explained as meaning "Maintain, perfectly, a state of mind where you are single-pointedly absorbed in the understanding that nothing is true."

rows.english: And what Lord Buddha is saying then is: "O Subhuti, every single object in the universe exists only through our projections; they have not a single atom of any other kind of existence—any natural existence. rows.wylie: mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa thob pas chos thams cad bden med du mngon sum du gzigs shing gang lung bstan pa dang thob par bya ba dang 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba thams cad kyang rang bzhin gyis stong par gzigs pas, mar me mdzad las bden grub kyi chos gang yang blangs snyam du zhen pa med do
rows.english: When one reaches the stage of the great mastery of things that never grow, one directly perceives that no object at all has any true existence. One perceives that what was predicted to finally happen, and the thing one is to achieve, and becoming enlightened—all of them—are empty of any natural existence. As such the Buddha had no belief that he was taking up any truly existing Dharma at all from the Buddha, Light Maker.

rows.acip: YANG DAG PA'I 'DU SHES ZHES BSHAD PA GANG YIN PA DE NI BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES MA MCHIS PA'I SLAD DU STE, DES NA BDEN ZHEN MED CING BDEN MED RTOGS PA'I 'DU SHES DE LA YANG DAG PA'I 'DU SHES ZHES DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS SO,,
rows.wylie: yang dag pa'i 'du shes zhes bshad pa gang yin pa de ni bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes ma mchis pa'i slad du ste, des na bden zhen med cing bden med rtogs pa'i 'du shes de la yang dag pa'i 'du shes zhes de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs so
rows.english: And this is because this same "correct thinking" is something that could never exist as a kind of thinking where one believed in things as being real. This is precisely why Those Gone Thus have used the expression "thinking correctly" to describe a kind of thinking where one no longer believes in things as being real: where one rather thinks in a way where they have realized that things have no reality.

rows.acip: NGAS BZOD PA'I 'KHOR GSUM BDEN MED DU SHES NAS BZOD PA BSGOMS PAS, THA SNYAD PA'I NGA LA DMIGS NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU BDAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES NAS GANG ZAG TU BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I 'DU SHES KYANG MA BYUNG
rows.wylie: ngas bzod pa'i 'khor gsum bden med du shes nas bzod pa bsgoms pas, tha snyad pa'i nga la dmigs nas nga'o snyam du bdag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes nas gang zag tu bden par zhen pa'i 'du shes kyang ma byung
rows.english: ZHING,At that moment I practiced patience, keeping my mind on an understanding of the lack of true existence to each of the three elements to the act of patience. As I focused on the "me" which exists nominally, there came into my mind no conception where I held any belief in some truly existing "me": and so I had no conception of anything from a truly existing "self" up to a truly existing "person."[320]

rows.english: On this idea that—if we entertain some belief in a self where we say to ourselves, "This is me, " we will begin as well to entertain thoughts of harming someone—the Commentary on Valid Perception states: Once there is a self,There is the idea of "other";And then we hold tightTo the "self" sideAnd we feel dislikeFor the "other" side.Once we become enmeshedIn these two different sides,Every other problem possibleThen starts to come to us.[106]

rows.acip: GAL TE DE LTA BU'I BLO ZHIG DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA YOD NA NI, DE NYID DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I BDAG DANG SEMS CAN DANG GANG ZAG DANG SROG TU BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA'I SKYON DU 'GYUR NA, DE NI MI RIGS TE, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA BDAG TU 'DZIN CING ZHEN PA SOGS MED PA'I PHYIR TE, DES BDAG TU 'DZIN PA'I MNGON ZHEN THAMS CAD SPANGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,If the One Thus Gone
rows.wylie: gal te de lta bu'i blo zhig de bzhin gshegs pa la yod na ni, de nyid de bzhin gshegs pa'i bdag dang sems can dang gang zag dang srog tu bden par 'dzin pa'i skyon du 'gyur na, de ni mi rigs te, de bzhin gshegs pa la bdag tu 'dzin cing zhen pa sogs med pa'i phyir te, des bdag tu 'dzin pa'i mngon zhen thams cad spangs pa'i phyir ro,,if The oNe thuS goNe
rows.english: ever did entertain this state of mind, there would be the problem that he would be grasping to some self of the One Gone Thus, and to some living being, or to some person, or else to something that lives, of the One Gone Thus. And that would be wrong, for the fact is that the One Gone Thus doesn't have any of these thoughts—any of this grasping to a self, or to any of the rest. This is because he has given up each and every form of the belief where we grasp to some self.[528]

rows.acip: MDOR NA, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA MING DANG GZUGS KYI SKUR BDEN PAR ZHEN PA'I BDEN 'DZIN GYIS BCINGS PA DE DAG NI, DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I CHOS KYI SKU LTA BA LA LOG PAR ZHUGS PA STE, SKYE BO DE DAG GIS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA NGA'I CHOS KYI SKU STONG PA NYID MI MTHONG NGO,,Which is to say—if we
rows.wylie: mdor na, de bzhin gshegs pa la ming dang gzugs kyi skur bden par zhen pa'i bden 'dzin gyis bcings pa de dag ni, de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos kyi sku lta ba la log par zhugs pa ste, skye bo de dag gis de bzhin gshegs pa nga'i chos kyi sku stong pa nyid mi mthong ngo,,which iS To Say—if we
rows.english: were to put it briefly—let us consider those who are shackled by the tendency to look upon the One Gone Thus and believe that he exists, in some real way, within either his name or his body of form. Such persons would be living in error as far as how they were viewing the reality body. People like this can't see me—that is, cannot see the reality body, or emptiness, that belongs to "me": to the One Gone Thus.[553]

rows.acip: DES NA THA SNYAD DU BSOD NAMS YONGS SU GZUNG BA ZHES BYA'O ZHES GSUNGS TE, 'DI'I GZUNG BAR MI BYA'O ZHES PAS BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO LA BDEN GRUB TU ZHEN PA'I RTAG LTA DANG, YONGS SU GZUNG MOD KYIS ZHES CHAD PAR
rows.wylie: des na tha snyad du bsod nams yongs su gzung ba zhes bya'o zhes gsungs te, 'di'i gzung bar mi bya'o zhes pas bsod nams kyi phung po la bden grub tu zhen pa'i rtag lta dang, yongs su gzung mod kyis zhes chad par
rows.english: LTA BA SEL LO,,And this is precisely why, Lord Buddha says, that—nominally speaking—we can call it "gathering the merit in." When the sutra says here that we are "not to gather," it is helping us to avoid the view that things are unchanging—where we believe that the mountains of merit exist in truth. When it says that we "should, of course, gather," then it is helping us to avoid the view that things have simply stopped. The Buddha neither comes nor goes

rows.english: You rush here and there in your worldly work; believe it is something worth something, but it sends you to pain. A dream you once had because of some random thoughts; a life of days and nights spent chasing a mirage.

rows.english: If in that hour you leave behind Even the name you used to be called, Then what need mention everything else? Oh here we are, me and the others of you Who perhaps are the same as me myself, Ignoring this one great terror to come, Completely engrossed in this life's affairs, Which having nothing to do with anything. Come please look after us, I pray, My Lama, look on us with love; We are every suffering person there is, And we have no one else to help us. * * * To Give Up Every Hope With this class we reach the final section in our review of the root bodhisattva vows.  This includes the last transgression of all, which is that unthinkable act of deciding that your will not one day become and enlightened Angel who can travel to all worlds and help all living beings.

rows.wylie: gzhug pa tsam la ni snod dang ldan mi ldan brtag mi dgos par gsungs te rtse mo las, de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi gsang ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi rgyal po chen po 'dir ni ma lus shing lus pa med pa'i sems can gyi khams thams cad 'jug tu rung ngo, ,snod dang snod ma yin pa yongs su brtag par mi bya ste, gzhug pa la mngon par zhen pa yongs su gzung bar bya'o, ,de ci'i phyir zhe na, sems can thams cad kyis mthong ba tsam gyi mod la phyir mi ldog pa nyid du 'gyur ro, ,dad pa med pa dang dge ba'i rtsa ba ma bsags pa dang rgyud yongs su ma smin pa dang mos pa med pa mang du zin kyang 'on kyang mthong ba tsam gyis so, ,zhes gsungs te dkyil 'khor du gzhug pa dang zhugs pa la dbang bskur ba gnyis las gzhug pa ni snod dang mi ldan pa la'ang ma bkag pa yin gyi dbang bskur ba mi 'gog pa ni min
rows.english: It is stated in scripture that--in a case where we are bringing the person into the secret world, and nothing more--then we need not examine them to see whether or not they are a proper vessel to actually fully enter into the secret teachings.  As the Tip of Diamond says, It is completely proper for every living being--each and every living being, of every different propensity--to enter into this great king, this secret world of all the Ones who have Gone To Bliss.  You need not perform that examination to see whether or not they are a worthy vessel; lead them in, anyone who has a true desire to do so. Why is this so?  Because in the very instant that any single living being in the entire universe lays eyes upon this world, the seed in them becomes totally unstoppable.  They may be someone who has a great many problems: they may be a person with no faith at all; or someone who has failed to collect any quantity of good karma at all; or whose heart is not at all ripened; or who simply has no interest in these things.  But still they become unstoppable, simply by laying eyes upon this world. And so there are two possibilities here: simply bringing someone into the secret world, or empowering them to enter the secret world.  The former of the two is not disallowed, even for those who are not a worthy vessel.  This is not of course to say that it is not disallowed to grant such a person empowerment. ***

rows.acip: SH'AN+TI PAS RTZOD PA'I DUS 'DIR 'GRO BA RNAMS BUD MED LA RAB TU ZHEN PAS, DE RNAMS GDUL PA'I PHYIR BUD MED DU SPRUL PA'I LHA RNAMS 'DI NA GNAS PAS MI SMOD CES SAM BUD MED KYI KHROD NA RDO RJE PHAG MO SOGS GNAS PAS DES NA GANG YIN MI SHES PAS BUD MED RNAMS LA MI SMOD PAR BZHED PA'I PHYIR BCAS PA'I SPYI MTSAMS 'DZIN PA LA BUD MED TZAM NAS BYED PAR GSAL LO,
rows.wylie: shAn+ti pas rtsod pa'i dus 'dir 'gro ba rnams bud med la rab tu zhen pas, de rnams gdul pa'i phyir bud med du sprul pa'i lha rnams 'di na gnas pas mi smod ces sam bud med kyi khrod na rdo rje phag mo sogs gnas pas des na gang yin mi shes pas bud med rnams la mi smod par bzhed pa'i phyir bcas pa'i spyi mtshams 'dzin pa la bud med tsam nas byed par gsal lo
rows.english: Shantipa here points out that "Here in the days of strife, people have a particular attachment to the female form; and so in order to tame these beings, Angels emanate as human women.  They are then here in the world with us, and we must never disparage Them."  So too we see, "Holy beings like the Diamond Sow are present here in the world, mixed among the human women.  As such, we never know which woman might be Them; and so we should never disparage women." Given this view of the vow, it is clear that the overall constraints of the rule refer only to women, [and not to men]. ***

rows.english: These lines are saying that one should live in such a way that you pass your hours with your Messenger, enjoying this sacred practice.  And you should do so "always," meaning constantly.  The practice should as well be done out of a love for the goal of reaching freedom.  You must, finally, assure that no one every ever leads you away from this particular path: and this then is the fourth of the pledges. ************

rows.wylie: snang ba de'i gnyen por dag pa'i rten dang brten par 'char ba'i snang ba dang , tha mal gyi zhen pa'i gnyen por dag pa'i rten dang brten pa'i nga rgyal sgom pa yin la, de yang nga rgyal sgom pa ni gtso bo dang , snang ba sgom pa ni de'i yan lag yin par gsungs so
rows.english: The antidote for things appearing as normal is to purposely bring to mind a world and its inhabitants which appear as totally pure.  The antidote for our tendency to see things as normal is to practice identifying ourselves with the divine, living in a divine world inhabited by beings who are divine.  It is stated that this identification with the divine is the main thing, and that bringing to mind the appearance of things as being pure is auxiliary to it.

rows.english: And this is the case because the speech here which is transcendent is the natural recitation: the three steps of the rising, the entering, and the staying of the inner winds.  And what we seek to transcend--the thing we wish to stop--is our tendency to believe that these three are somehow things which are different from the song of the three syllables.  The essence of transcendence here then is where the song of the rising, the entering, and the staying of the winds is joined indivisibly with the song of the three syllables.

rows.english: And the Dark Man says to Him, The wild deer Of holding that what we see And the one that sees it Both come from themselves Is racing up the mountain Of our bodies: our tendency To think they must be "me". I am the Hunter Who wants nothing more Than the kill: I take the arrow Of the rainbow body, The belief that nothing Is as it seems, And I use the bow Of the state of being In clear and simple light. Seek me then tomorrow, The fisherman At the ocean's shore. And with this He disappears.  And so the next day Naropa is walking still, praying still, seeking still.

rows.english: Here then is the second part from above: actually carrying out the directions.  This too has two parts.  The first is keeping your mind on identifying with Her, and the second is keeping your mind on looking like Her; here is the first.  It is true that you need to see yourself as Her, but the most important thing is to feel like Her, because--as they say--you aren't fettered by how you look, by rather by what you believe.  What this is saying is that we are fettered to circle of pain by our belief that things are normal; therefore we must practice seeing our heaps, categories, and gateways as the Angel of Diamond.

rows.acip: THA MAL PA'I SNANG BA YID NGOR DAG PAR BYED NUS PA YIN LA, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I BCOS MIN GYI NGA RGYAL 'PHO NUS PA BYUNG BA NA, THA MAL PA'I ZHEN PA YID NGOR DAG PAR BYED NUS PA YIN NO,,

rows.english: At this stage we say that you have reached the capacity to purify your mind of any tendency to see things as normal. rows.acip: 'GRO BA CHAGS PAS MYOS SHING, DE LA ZHEN PA RNAMS 'DUL BA'I SLAD DU RNAL 'BYOR MA MI MO'I RNAM PAS BUD MED KYI KHROD DU BYON TE RGYUD BYIN GYIS RLOB PA SOGS KYIS DNGOS GRUB LHAG PAR MYUR BA'I KHYAD CHOS TE KHYAD CHOS GSUM

rows.english: Finally, these are times when beings are crazed with desire; and because She also wants to help those who have a craving for that sort of thing, the Angel comes to us in the form of a human female, mixing with the women of the world, so She can give Her blessings to our being. rows.acip: LAS KYI PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN NAS 'JUG PA'I TSUL LA PHYAG RGYA'I MTSAN NYID BRTAG THABS, DE 'KHOR BA LA ZHEN PA LOG NAS THAR PA THOB 'DOD KYI BLO BCOS MA MA YIN PA BSKYED DE, BYAMS SNYING RJE BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSKYED,

rows.english: Concerning the method where we get the winds to enter by practicing with an actual partner, there are first of all certain ways of examining a potential partner to see if they possess the requisite characteristics.  They must have gained an aversion for this cycle of pain; they must have reached an uncontrived state of mind where they truly hope to attain freedom from this suffering.  And they must as well have developed within themselves the attitudes of love, compassion, and the Wish for enlightenment.

rows.acip: SH'ANTI PAS RTZOD PA'I DUS 'DIR 'GRO BA RNAMS BUD MED LA RAB TU ZHEN PAS, DE RNAMS GDUL PA'I PHYIR BUD MED DU SPRUL PA'I LHA RNAMS 'DI NA GNAS PAS MI SMOD CES SAM BUD MED KYI KHROD NA RDO RJE PHAG MO SOGS GNAS PAS DES NA GANG YIN MI SHES PAS BUD MED RNAMS LA MI SMOD PAR BZHED PA'I PHYIR BCAS PA'I SPYI MTSAMS 'DZIN PA LA BUD MED TZAM NAS BYED PAR GSAL LO, ,
rows.wylie: shAnti pas rtsod pa'i dus 'dir 'gro ba rnams bud med la rab tu zhen pas, de rnams gdul pa'i phyir bud med du sprul pa'i lha rnams 'di na gnas pas mi smod ces sam bud med kyi khrod na rdo rje phag mo sogs gnas pas des na gang yin mi shes pas bud med rnams la mi smod par bzhed pa'i phyir bcas pa'i spyi mtshams 'dzin pa la bud med tsam nas byed par gsal lo,
rows.english: Shantipa here points out that "Here in the days of strife, people have a particular attachment to the female form; and so in order to tame these beings, Angels emanate as human women.  They are then here in the world with us, and we must never disparage Them."  So too we see, "Holy beings like the Diamond Sow are present here in the world, mixed among the human women.  As such, we never know which woman might be Them; and so we should never disparage women." * * * The famed Fifty Verses on Lamas by Master Ashvaghosha (c. 150 AD) is a source of a great number of our secret vows and pledges.  Je Rinpoche relates one of these to partner practice; we first hear the vow itself, from Geshe Tsewang Samdrup's String of Shining Jewels (ACIP digital text S00201, f. 24a), and then read Je Tsongkapa's comments on it, from His Elucidation of the "Fifty Verses on Lamas" (ACIP digital text S05269, f. 19a).

rows.english: It's important to say here that—when we talk about clarity, or clearness—we're not talking about a quality of the object. Rather, it's a distinction that you have to make about the subject state of mind in meditation: does the mind itself feel clear—is there mental clarity, or not? When we can't get clarity to come, it feels almost like we've moved under a dark shadow.
